cases.quote: The intent of widow adjustment of paragraphs is to avoid that the last line of a paragraph contains less than a given number of characters. This is also called "widow" processing.
cases.rationale: `standing: "normative"`, not `"unstated"`: this format reserves `unstated`/`adjudicated`/`alternative` for a case whose `permitted` records more than one reachable answer (`conform --check`'s own `check_standing`, ADR-0006), and nothing in this workspace's `Policy` selects the exempting reading Q2 rejects below — there is no second reachable answer for a second `permitted` entry to carry, only the one this case states and the one `forbidden` excludes. This case's own central claim is §3.5.4's own stated rule applied to this fixture through `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q2 reading of what 'the last line of a paragraph' leaves open, the same way `3.1.12.json`'s own cases stay `normative` while reading a scope decision onto a worked example. §3.5.4's own words name 'the last line of a paragraph' without excluding the paragraph whose only line is also its last — read literally, as Q2 argues, a one-line paragraph's own single line is that paragraph's own last line, and nothing in the quoted sentence carries a condition that would except it. `亜亜` (two full-em ideographs, 1000 units each on a 1000-unit em) is set with no candidates at all: `jlreq_line::Candidate`'s own doc states 'the last line ends where the text does, whether or not a candidate says so,' so this text composes to exactly one line covering both items regardless of the empty `candidates` array. That line's own natural extent is the sum of its two items' advances, 1000 + 1000 = 2000, with `measure` set to 2500 so the line sits short of the target without ever being overfull — under §3.8.1's Note the paragraph's own last line is exempt from expansion, so this line's own placements stay at the natural `[0, 1000]` and its extent stays 2000 rather than being padded out toward 2500, and nothing on it is trimmed, so `trims` is asserted empty. The line's own item count — `end.get() - start.get()` over its `ItemIndex` range, `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q1 reading of 'a character' — is 2. `widow_threshold: 3` asks for more than this only line carries, so under Q2's literal reading `jlreq_line::compose` reports a `ViolationKind::Widow` naming this rule, and `violations: ["3.5.4"]` is the whole of what changes here: the geometry is identical to what the same paragraph composes with no threshold at all (`Paragraph::with_widow_threshold`'s own doc states a threshold of 0 is a no-op by construction), because `Search::FirstFit` never compares arrangements and setting the threshold only makes the shortfall of the one line it already chose observable, through the identical violation, the same doc's own words. A non-empty `lines` beside a real violation is itself this case's own piece of evidence for Q4: `jlreq_line::compose` still produced a full composition for a paragraph whose declared threshold nothing in this fixture could satisfy, rather than refusing the input outright — the graceful-degradation-plus-honest-violation pattern ADR-0010 states for every unsatisfiable constraint this crate reports, which `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q4 applies here by name.

forbidden.why: The exempting alternative Q2 names and rejects: a one-line paragraph read as exempt from widow adjustment because it has no earlier line to be short relative to. §3.5.4's own sentence states no such exemption — it names only "the last line of a paragraph," not "the last line of a paragraph of more than one line" — so answering `violations: []` for this identical input invents a condition the specification does not state, exactly the invention `docs/decisions/README.md` exists to forbid; `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q2 argues the point by name and at length.

cases.quote: The intent of widow adjustment of paragraphs is to avoid that the last line of a paragraph contains less than a given number of characters. This is also called "widow" processing.
cases.rationale: `standing: "normative"`, for the reason its sibling case above states in full: this case has one reachable answer, not a second a `Policy` question could select, so `conform --check`'s own `check_standing` (ADR-0006) is the reason this is `normative` rather than `unstated` even though the counting unit it turns on is a published reading of a silence. This case and the one below turn on `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q1, kumihan's published reading of what 'a character' counts as, not on a sentence §3.5.4 states outright. Q1 reads a character as an item — `end.get() - start.get()` over the line's own `ItemIndex` range, the one granularity this workspace counts by anywhere (ADR-0008) — and this pair of cases (this one and its sibling immediately below) is built so the last line's own item count diverges from both its code-point count and its byte count, so an implementation counting either of those instead would answer this identical input differently from one that counts items. The paragraph is four items: two full-em ideographs (`亜`, 1000 units each) followed by two Western-letter clusters on the proportional frame, `fi` and `if`, 700 units each — both letters `f` and `i`, the pair Appendix A literally lists under cl-27, the same two letters `jlreq_class::Text`'s own Western-ligature test proves the exception with (`ffi`, ADR-0018's own carve-out for a proportional multi-code-point cluster that is a Western ligature and nothing else). `fi` is one item covering two code points (bytes 6-8); `if` is a second item covering two more (bytes 8-10) — four code points and four bytes on the last line against two items, the divergence this pair exists to pin. The sole candidate this case offers is the boundary after the second ideograph, byte offset 6; `jlreq_line::Candidate`'s own doc states the paragraph's own last line always ends where the text does regardless of what candidates say, so with only one interior candidate offered, `Search::FirstFit` has no other break to take: line 1 is items 0-1 (`亜亜`, 1000 + 1000 = 2000, exactly `measure`, so neither reduced nor expanded — badness zero, nothing trimmed), and line 2, the last line, is items 2-3 (`fi` then `if`, 700 + 700 = 1400). `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table1.rs`'s own cell at cl-27 before cl-27 — the interior boundary between the two Western items — carries `terms: &[]`, so the two sit solid: line 2's own placements are `[0, 700]` and its extent is 1400, short of the 2000-unit measure but, as the paragraph's own last line, exempt from expansion under §3.8.1's Note rather than padded out toward it, and nothing on it is trimmed either. Line 2's own item count is 2. `widow_threshold: 2` asks for no more than this line already carries, so `have (2) < want (2)` is false and no violation is reported: `violations: []` is this pair's own baseline, the boundary value the sibling case immediately below crosses.

cases.quote: The intent of widow adjustment of paragraphs is to avoid that the last line of a paragraph contains less than a given number of characters. This is also called "widow" processing.
cases.rationale: The identical paragraph, byte for byte, `3.5.4/last-line-item-count/a-threshold-equal-to-the-count-is-satisfied` above reads, with `widow_threshold` raised from 2 to 3 — one past the last line's own item count. `standing: "normative"` for the same reason as its sibling: one reachable answer, no second `Policy`-selectable reading for a second `permitted` entry to name, so `conform --check`'s own `check_standing` (ADR-0006) holds this to `normative` even though this pins Q1's own counting unit, kumihan's own published reading of §3.5.4's silence. Nothing about the composed geometry changes: `Paragraph::with_widow_threshold`'s own doc states that `Search::FirstFit` never compares arrangements, so it never moves a break in response to this field, and the sole offered candidate still forces the identical 2+2 split the sibling case's own rationale derives in full (line 1: items 0-1, `亜亜`, exactly 2000 units against `measure`; line 2, the last line: items 2-3, `fi` then `if`, 1400 units, solid at the cl-27x cl-27 boundary Table 1 states no term at). What changes is only the comparison the threshold asks of that unchanged last line: `have (2) < want (3)` now holds, so `jlreq_line::compose` reports a `ViolationKind::Widow` naming this rule, and `violations: ["3.5.4"]` is the whole of what this case adds over its sibling. Read against the sibling as a pair, this is the discriminating half Q1 needs: an implementation counting this last line by code point (4) or by byte (4) would answer this identical input `violations: []`, the sibling's own answer, because either count still meets a threshold of 3 — only item-counting (2) crosses it, which is what this pair actually rules out, code-point counting and byte counting together, rather than byte counting alone. That `jlreq_line::compose` still returns both lines in full here, rather than refusing the paragraph outright, is this rule's own second piece of evidence for Q4 (the first is the sibling case's own single-line fixture at a different threshold entirely): a caller-declared threshold this fixture's own last line cannot reach is met with graceful degradation and an honest violation, never a refusal, exactly ADR-0010's own stated pattern for every unsatisfiable constraint this crate reports, which `docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q4 applies here by name.
